subject: Post-call: Parallelization & SLO follow-up (concurrency + rate limits)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Wong <ellie@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Parallelization & SLO follow-up (concurrency + rate limits)

Hi Ellie,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear context on Nimbus Retail's real-time recommendations use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call recap (top of mind)
- Goal: Embed product recommendations in checkout and browse in sub-200ms median for UX-critical rendering; streaming results for incremental UI updates.
- Load profile: peak campaign windows ~1,000 parallel users concurrently generating 2–3 streaming completions each (average sequence length ~120 tokens). Outside campaign windows, steady-state ~150 concurrent users.
- p95 latency target: 150ms for short streaming responses, 300ms p95 for long completions.
- SLOs we should validate: 95th latency, 50k tokens/min throughput during peak bursts, and max parallel request concurrency ~1,000 (across your front-end fleet).

Immediate asks we agreed to:
1) Confirmation of whether front-end will multiplex requests over TLS connections (keepalive) or open new connections per tab. This affects required connection pool sizing.
2) Whether all sessions must be isolated per customer (per-tenant KV cache) or can share global cache for prefix reuse.
3) Procurement note: a PO path and any special billing terms (cc'd procurement).

What I propose next from Redwood: 
- Technical proposal (attached SLO_Redwood_Technical_Spec.pdf) with two options: Hosted with raised per-route quotas + burst tokens OR Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) with guaranteed concurrency floor.
- Initial rate/quota config we think matches your call: per-API-key baseline 200 rps, burstable to 1,200 rps in 60s windows using token-bucket tapering; connection pool suggestion: 250 keepalive connections per region, max concurrent streams per connection = 6 (we can tune).
- Quick benchmark: 48-hour window where Nimbus will run a 2–3 hour synthetic campaign test and we’ll capture p50/p95/p99, KV hit rates, and per-token cost delta across quantization profiles.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Reply with definitive answers to items (1) and (2) above.
- Confirm interest in Hosted-burst vs Dedicated reserved capacity for us to produce a cost estimate.
- Suggested window for benchmark (we were thinking Oct 14–15).

Attachments: SLO_Redwood_Technical_Spec.pdf (technical knobs + proposed quota table).

Thanks — I’ll loop Camila and Hannah internally to draft the config options and cost delta.

Best,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference for engineering teams

From: Ellie Wong <ellie@nimbusretail.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Parallelization & SLO follow-up (concurrency + rate limits)

Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. A few clarifications below: 

1) Front-end behavior: we multiplex requests from each browser session using a shared keepalive pool (managed by our CDN edge workers). We aim to keep TLS connections open and reuse them.
2) Cache isolation: we prefer isolated per-customer logical namespaces for privacy, but are open to shared global prefix caching for non-sensitive lookups (recommendation prefetches).
3) Procurement: we can accept standard Redwood PO terms; procurement has asked for a sample PO template (attached).

Quick note on numbers: 
- Campaign peak: the 1,000 parallel users is accurate but plan for 30% geographic concurrency (east/west US).
- Streaming requirement: UI must receive the first token within 80–120ms; incremental token arrival thereafter can be best-effort so long as p95 of first token < 200ms.

We’re happy to run a benchmark Oct 14–15. Please send the benchmark harness and example load profile.

Ellie

--
Ellie Wong
Director, Engineering — Real-time Platform
Nimbus Retail
ellie@nimbusretail.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Parallelization & SLO follow-up (concurrency + rate limits)

Hi team — draft proposal for Nimbus (summary below). I’m keeping technical detail tight for procurement and adding a separate appendix for the benchmark harness.

Option A — Hosted (fastest TTV)
- Per-API-key steady quota: 200 rps (requests/sec).
- Token-bucket burst: +1,000 rps for 60s windows (burst tokens = 60k per minute window) with tapering to baseline over next 180s.
- Connection pool guidance: keepalive sockets = 250 per-edge-region; max concurrent streams per connection = 6 (so theoretical concurrency = 1,500 per region).
- Streaming specifics: first-token p95 SLO: 200ms; per-token throughput SLA for sustained streams: 20 tokens/sec per session (configurable).
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a compatible quantized variant under heavy load; degraded mode returns compact single-shot responses if streaming violates SLO.
- Price guidance: incremental hosted cost estimate for peak campaign (2 hours, 50k tokens/min peak) = $Xk (detailed line items in appendix).

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity, stronger guarantees)
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs in US regions with pinned model variant (gptr-compact-8q).
- Guaranteed concurrency floor: 1,200 concurrent requests across pool; burst up to 3,000 by borrowing burst credits from cross-customer pool (with advance notice).
- Connection pool: dedicated keepalive endpoints; recommended sockets = 400; per-connection streams = 8.
- SLA: p95 streaming-first-token 150ms (measured during benchmark windows), 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints.
- Pricing: monthly reserved commitment + overage by token.

Benchmark plan (Oct 14–15)
- Redwood provides a benchmark harness (k6 + custom stream simulator) and a small client-side snippet to reproduce multiplexing behavior.
- We’ll measure p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit-rate, and tail latencies across regions (east/west) + CPU/GPU utilization.
- Deliverables: full report, suggested tuning (keepalive pool, per-connection stream cap, quantization changes).

Next steps I recommend we send Ellie a short options email and a cost appendix, then book a 30-min technical deep-dive to align the benchmark harness.

Attaching the technical appendix to the thread and will upload the harness link after internal sign-off.

Camila

--

2) Dedicated (recommended if you need firm guarantees during campaigns): reserved pool with 1,200 guaranteed concurrency, burst to 3,000, dedicated keepalive endpoints (400 sockets), per-connection streams=8. SLA available.

Rishi
